segments.narration: A massive metallic heartbeat echoed against US submarine hulls. Back in 1970, elite sonar crews off the coast of California detected something impossible: a rhythmic, mechanical thumping coming from the absolute pitch black of the deep ocean.

Every single day at the exact same hour, the pulse returned. It wasn't whale song, and it wasn't seismic activity. It sounded like heavy machinery operating miles beneath the surface where no machine had any business being.
Could a rogue submarine really hide down there for months without leaving a single wake?

Naval investigators finally cracked the source after tracking the acoustic signature right to its doorstep. It wasn't a foreign sub at all. It was a secret marine research facility pumping compressed air into the seabed to test underwater acoustics.
The terrifying deep-sea heartbeat was just a high-tech air compressor. What happens when our own machinery starts sounding like an alien lifeform in the dark?
